To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the semi-empiric method PM6 is an efficient tool for estimation of log KOAs of PCt- ABs and can be recommended as a reliable and time saving method for estimation of log KOs of PCt- and other polychlorinated aromatic compounds.
the PM6 method is a reliable tool to estimate log KOA values in the range from 8.3 to 13.5, which is in a good agreement with experimental log KOA values.
the log KOA values for the 209 PCtABs have been determined by two computational approaches (PM6 and DFT) and that the values of these log KOAs are in the range from 8.30 to 13.49.
In summary, our research is concerned with
determination of the log KOA values for all 209 PC-ABs.
determination of log KOA values and classification of the environmental mobility of PCt- ABs.
the estimation of log KOAs for all 209 PCts-ABs, and it will be useful for the prediction of the distribution and transport of these compounds in the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the log KOA values for the 209 investigated PCt- ABs are in the range of 8.30-13.49.

the log KOA of the investigated PC-ABs is a strong function of their chemical structure, and the log KOA values are highly dependent on the number of chlorine atoms and their positions in the molecule.
PCt-AB compounds are of low to medium mobility in the environment, which is consistent with the results reported in the literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the computational methods are able to predict the log KOA values for PCt-AB congeners.
the PM6 method is a very useful and reliable computational tool to estimate log KOA partition coefficient of the 209 PCt–ABs.
PM6 is a very good alternative to DFT for estimation of log KOAs of PCt- ABs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PM6 and DTF methods are reliable and can be used to predict environmental mobility and adsorption of PCt- ABs.

the computational chemistry methods, such as PM6 and DTF methods, can be used to predict the log KOA values and to fill the gaps in environmental relevant physical and chemical property data of PCt-ABS.

PCt-AB homologue groups can be ranked according to their log KOA values and classified as low (Mono-, and some of Di-Ct-AB) to high environmental mobility (most Tri- to Nono-Ct-AB and Deca-CAB homologues).
